title: A bill to designate the General George C. Marshall House, in the Commonwealth of Virginia, as an affiliated area of the National Park System, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
This bill establishes the General George C. Marshall House in Leesburg, Virginia, as an affiliated area of the National Park System to promote public appreciation of the historic contributions made by George Catlett Marshall, Jr. (George Catlett Marshall, Jr. served as Army Chief of Staff during World War II, and later as Secretary of State, president of the American Red Cross, and Secretary of Defense.)

The bill designates the George C. Marshall International Center as the management entity for the affiliated area. The Department of the Interior must enter into an agreement with the center that describes the roles and responsibilities for management of the affiliated area. Further, Interior may provide technical assistance and enter into cooperative agreements with the center for the purpose of providing financial assistance for the marketing, marking, interpretation, and preservation of the affiliated area.

summary.headline: New law makes the General George C. Marshall House in Leesburg, Virginia, an affiliated area of the National Park System.
summary.what_it_does: The law names the George C. Marshall House in Leesburg, Virginia, as an affiliated area of the National Park System to honor the life of George C. Marshall, who led the Army in World War II and later served as Secretary of State and Secretary of Defense. The George C. Marshall International Center will manage the site, not the National Park Service. The Department of the Interior must sign an agreement with the center that spells out who handles what. Interior may also give the center technical help and money for marketing, signs, educational programs, and preservation.

who_it_affects.how: The center becomes the official manager of the site and may receive federal technical help and funding through cooperative agreements.
The department must sign a management agreement with the center and may choose to provide technical and financial assistance.
The house gains National Park System affiliation, which may bring added signs, educational programs, and promotion.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary gives no separate start date, so it likely took effect when signed on September 25, 2026.
